facts.text: Gold Hill was founded in 1859 during the Colorado Gold Rush, becoming the first mining district in the region.
The town’s oldest continuously operating public school, the two‑room Gold Hill School, opened in 1873 and still serves students today.
A 1930s mining boom brought tellurium to Gold Hill, linking the town’s history to a rare element that once powered early radio technology.
The Bluebird Organization, active in the early 1900s, helped preserve Gold Hill’s historic buildings and foster community events that still echo today.
Gold Hill’s historic wooden structures survived two major fires, and many have been restored, giving the town a preserved 19th‑century feel.
Perched at 8,300 feet above Left Hand Canyon, Gold Hill’s narrow dirt roads become impassable in winter unless vehicles have chains or four‑wheel drive.
